analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. It adds one env-var row at docs/reference/configuration.md:417 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, a new benchmark report docs/reports/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup-first-request.md, and an index entry plus date bump in docs/reports/README.md. No source code, authorization, attestation, crypto, or cache-storage behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Threat-model checks:
- The new knob is a load-time shader-cache warmup. The doc says it trains no rate or counter and is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. It touches no A-001 prompt data, A-003 keys, A-015/A-016 authorization, or the TB-002 wire contract.
- Prefix-cache handling (T-041): the benchmark method states prefix cache was off and each prompt began with a unique nonce, so no prefix was reused. The report makes no claim that changes the SEC-035 TTFT oracle acceptance. The warmup lowers first-request latency on a cold Metal shader cache, which could marginally reduce a cold-start timing signal, but the doc claims nothing about this.
- The report is evidence, not a qualification claim. It cites a throwaway bundle ID used to simulate a cold cache and a binary MD5. It states limitations: two models, one prompt length, no concurrent-load measurement. Nothing in it asserts a production qualification or policy change.
- Open question for a later pass: the implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (shapeWarmupMode) is not in the supplied evidence. Whether the warmup path handles inputs safely, and whether the `always` value skipping the probe has any security-relevant effect, was not verified. The doc references cold-cache margins (250 ms vs 750 ms) that cannot be checked here. The cited evidence files under evidence/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup/ were not supplied.

No regressions or invalidated threat assumptions were identified from the docs alone.
